content: I am new to Lean and I created https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/40973. I used Lean to prove some theorems and derivations in my personal notes (deriving determinants from a homomorphism) and Lean was able to check and prove everything, it's amazing. Now I have so many other ideas that I would like to formalize. Thank you all for your work on this. I extracted theorems that I felt could be part of Mathlib and that's the PR above. Let me know if you think this is in scope and how to improve it. I added one file and modified another, do you want me to split it into two PRs?

Hi Ondřej, great to see some more people coming from sympy! Mathlib tends to be reluctant to review AI-generated proofs from new contributors, especially long ones. Having said that, your changes to the the existing file look very easy to review, and I'd be happy to merge them if you split that out to a separate PR
@Eric Wieser thank you! I split it: https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/40976

Yes, I totally understand regarding AI. On the positive side, if it wasn't for AI, I wouldn't even attempt using Lean, it would take me weeks or months to figure out if it can prove what I needed. AI did it instantly using Mathlib (it turns out all the building blocks are already there), and it found a bug in my manual derivation, I prove it for R but not C. And that is actually the PR above, it turns out it can be done, but it's not even in Mathlib yet, and it took Opus 4.8 about 1h, but it figured it out. Consequently, it might not be good enough to merge, but it compiles, so the theorem works, which is just amazing.

I will now try to use Lean to formalize many of my other notes, literally until a few days ago I didn't know this field advanced so much that I can actually use it. It's incredible. Once I learn Lean better, I can resubmit the PR later, or somebody else can prove it properly. It's not a blocker at all for me, I can just have this file in my own project. I just thought it would save others time if this theorem was already included, but I do not want to increase the technical debt either.

For the sake of zulip search, I'll repeat your main result here:

/-- **Automatic continuity of measurable additive characters on `ℝ`.** A Borel-measurable additive
character `ψ : AddChar ℝ 𝕜` (`RCLike 𝕜`) is continuous. This is the multiplicative companion of
`MeasureTheory.Measure.AddMonoidHom.continuous_of_measurable`; at `𝕜 = ℂ` it gives the automatic
continuity of measurable characters `ℝ → ℂ`. -/
theorem AddChar.continuous_of_measurable {ψ : AddChar ℝ 𝕜} (hmeas : Measurable ψ) :
    Continuous ψ :=
  continuous_of_measurable_of_mul hmeas ψ.map_add_eq_mul
